_readme: Model prices, as data rather than as constants in code.
Every price is a STRING, never a JSON number. json.load() turns a bare 0.75
into a float, which would reintroduce exactly the imprecision that
ci_triage.money exists to prevent. Strings parse to Decimal exactly.
fetched_at is not decoration. A price table with no date cannot be audited,
and a silently stale table under-estimates cost -- the one direction a
budget estimate must never be wrong in. Re-check the source URLs and bump
fetched_at; do not edit prices without doing both.
chars_per_token is the conservative characters-per-token ratio used to turn
a log into an upper bound on tokens. It is MEASURED, not assumed: see
tools/measure_token_density.py. The familiar '4 characters per token' is a
figure for English prose and understates real CI log content by up to 4.6x.
